text:
Jules: Quick sync: Product wants a "cache savings heatmap" in the cost dashboard. Should it be per-route or per-model-hotpath?
Priya: per-route primary, with a model-level drilldown. Routes are what tenants think about for billing.
Omar: Agreed. Heatmap should show absolute tokens saved and pct of route burn. Color by absolute then stroke by pct.
Lin: UX nit: add a toggle to switch units (tokens / $approx / credits) so customers can view dollars. We'll need a conversion table for model SKUs.
Jules: Implementation decision: compute savings by summing amortized cache credits from slabs vs naive uncached token estimate. Precompute vs compute-on-demand?
Priya: Precompute hourly slabs for UI. On-demand recompute for ad-hoc ranges in the drilldown. Avoid heavy joins in the main dashboard query.
Omar: We'll need to handle multi-model chains where prefix cache is applied on different SKUs. Attribution rule: attribute saved tokens to the route that initiated the chain, then break down by model in drilldown.
Lin: CSV export is a blocker for support teams. Endpoint should return both heatmap matrix and a flattened CSV with columns: route, slab_hour, token_saved, sample_rate, model_sku.
Jules: API proto sketch (for drilldown):
```
GET /api/v1/costs/route/:route_id/cache_savings?start=..&end=..&granularity=hour&format=json
Response: rows [{"slab_hour":..., "model_sku":"...", "token_saved":..., "sample_rate":...}]
```
Priya: Also need to expose the precompute job status in telemetry. If slabs fail, fallback to a sampled recompute that is flagged in UI.
cost-bot: alert: route_cache_slabs_job_failed count=3 in the last hour. Check /ops/jobs/route_cache_slabs for logs.
Omar: Good call. UI should surface stale data banner when slab job hasn't run for >2 hours.
Lin: For canary rollouts we want to compare savings per-model-variant. UX: side-by-side heatmaps + a delta layer that shows percent change and a significance tag (t-test p<0.05) for high-volume routes.
Jules: Significance testing on sparse routes is noisy. Make tests opt-in per-tenant (default off) and only run for routes with >N tokens in window.
Priya: Retention question: keep hourly slabs for 30 days in hot storage, then aggregate to daily for 12 months. That balances query cost and long-term billing reconciliation.
Omar: Agree. Also add a sample_rate column for each slab so users understand downsampling. Without that it's misleading.
Lin: Edge-case: prefetch credits that later become invalid due to model fallback. Need to annotate those slabs as "reconciled=false" and exclude from billing exports until reconciled.
Jules: We'll add a reconciliation pass that marks slabs reconciled when chain outcome settles. Export API will include reconciled flag and will default to excluding unreconciled unless `include_unreconciled=true`.
Priya: Tests: include vectors for multi-model chain with mixed sample rates, heavy-prefetch that warms cache across SKUs, and a canary split with model-variant B at 10% traffic.
Omar: For the heatmap UI performance: client should pull precomputed matrix and render via WebGL if matrix > 200x200. Otherwise SVG is fine.
Lin: Accessibility: ensure colorblind-safe palette and numeric overlays available. Also keyboard nav to drill into a cell.
Jules: I'll write the RFC with API shape, precompute job spec, and telemetry signals (job success/failure, slab_age, reconciled_count). Priya will review.
Priya: I'll draft the CSV contract and the billing export example. Also adding an ops playbook entry for stale slabs.
Omar: I'll implement the precompute worker and reconciliation pass. Feature flag `ui.cache_heatmap_enable` gated per-tenant.
Lin: I'll produce mocks and the canary delta interaction. Delivery target: EOW for prototype in staging.
Jules: Thx team. Drop any more edgecases here (sessions that span window boundaries, slab clock-skew).
Priya: note: include timezone-normalized slab_hour in UTC and tenant_local_hour for display.
Omar: logging: include route_id, slab_hour, job_run_id in all slab writes for traceability.
Lin: +1. Posting mocks to #product-mockups shortly.
Jules: moving to action items.
